chunks: From him, from his father, from Al-Qasim ibn Muhammad Al-Jawhari, from Habib Al-Khash'ami, from Abdullah ibn Abi Yafour, who said:
I heard Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) saying: 'asws ) saying: 'When the man has no sense of honour (ghayrah), he is of an inverted heart.'

key_terms.الْغَيْرَة: Sense of honour, modesty, or jealousy in a positive moral sense
key_terms.مَنْكُوسُ الْقَلْبِ: Inverted heart, indicating a distorted or deficient spiritual state

ai.seo_question: What does it mean to have an inverted heart in Shia ethics?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, 'ghayrah' is viewed not merely as jealousy but as a divine instinct for protecting one's dignity and faith; its absence signifies a 'mankus al-qalb' (inverted heart), where the core of one's moral compass is distorted. This condition reflects a disconnection from the natural disposition (fitrah) that aligns the heart with God's attributes, rendering the individual vulnerable to moral decay and spiritual blindness.
